## Storage decision boundary

No host loop devices is unconditional, including pool backing and seed views. Existing loops are conflicts, not exemptions or permission to detach them. Native Incus Btrfs filesystem volumes are subvolumes, not writable block members for Btrfs sprouting. Subvolume-only storage cannot be called equivalent merely because it preserves files. Retain actual immutable-seed ancestry, persistent private writes, upgrade replication and root composition unless the owner explicitly changes those semantics.

The saved feasibility investigation quotes the upstream Linux 6.17+ restriction on mounting the same seed device both independently and through sprouts. An authorized non-loop writable allocation alone does not resolve the permanent standalone-seed mount requirement. This is an unresolved prerequisite, not proof that all possible native Incus integrations are impossible.
